label: early copy phase: second (and for long sequences third) output step
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase: never on original tokens, weakly on the <DEL> step (5% of mass), and mainly on the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, 68% of mass, active in 39% of sequences) and the step after that (recall_idx 2, 26%). It is essentially silent from recall_idx 3 onward. Rate and mass increase with sequence length (L=9 holds 42% of mass), and recall_idx 2 activations come mostly from L >= 7. Inside this window, whether it fires and how strongly depends on token identity. It is strongest when the token being output is h, b, f, z, l or r (or the next output is z, h, f or b) and when the input is a digit 3/2 or y, t, p, b, q. The top examples are all recall_idx 1 with inputs such as c, q, 3, 2 and outputs b, h or f. The positional predicate captures about 92% of the mass but only about 37% precision, because most early-copy steps with other tokens stay below threshold. Token lists push F1 to about 0.6 but are ad hoc.
